record.paper_title: Known Results and Open Problems on C1 linearization in Banach Spaces
record.context_brief: Role of Jordan blocks and selfadjointness
record.original_question: The known counterexamples to C^1 linearization described in this paper use an infinite-dimensional Jordan block in the linear part. Is such a Jordan-block structure actually necessary for counterexamples? More specifically, can one build counterexamples in which the linear part A is selfadjoint; and if that is impossible, can the spectral non-resonance condition (2) be improved when A is selfadjoint, or more generally when A is normal?

evidence.quote: Problem 2: Jordan blocks. Our counterexamples have an infinite-dimensional Jordan block. Is this necessary? Can one have counterexamples with a selfadjoint linear part A? If this is not the case, can one improve (2) if A is selfadjoint, or even normal?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $X$ be a real or complex Banach space and let $A : X 	o X$ be a bounded linear operator whose spectrum $\sigma(A)$ is hyperbolic, i.e. $\sigma(A) \cap \{z \in \mathbb{C} : |z| = 1\} = \emptyset$. Consider a $C^1$ map $T : X 	o X$ of the form
$$T(x) = A x + f(x),$$
where $f : X 	o X$ is $C^1$, $f(0) = 0$, $Df(0) = 0$, and $f$ together with $Df$ is bounded on $X$ (or, equivalently, one considers a local diffeomorphism near $0$ with $T(0)=0$, $DT(0)=A$).

The map $T$ is said to be $C^1$ linearizable (near $0$) if there exists a $C^1$ diffeomorphism $H$ defined on a neighborhood of $0$ in $X$ with $H(0)=0$ such that
$$H \circ T = A \circ H$$
on a neighborhood of $0$.

Assume the following spectral non-resonance condition on the spectrum $\sigma(A) = \sigma_s \cup \sigma_u$ (the splitting into stable part $\sigma_s \subset \{|z|<1\}$ and unstable part $\sigma_u \subset \{|z|>1\}$): there exist constants $a, b, A_u, B_u$ with
$$0 < a \le |\lambda| \le b < 1 \quad 	ext{for all } \lambda \in \sigma_s, \qquad 1 < A_u \le |\mu| \le B_u \quad 	ext{for all } \mu \in \sigma_u,$$
and the non-resonance gap
$$b < a^2, \qquad A_u > B_u^{1/2}$$
holds (this is the standard spectral non-resonance condition (∗) used to obtain $C^1$ linearization).

It is known that there exist $C^1$ maps $T$ on infinite-dimensional Banach spaces, with hyperbolic linear part $A$, for which no $C^1$ linearization exists; all such known counterexamples use a linear part $A$ that contains an infinite-dimensional Jordan block (i.e., $A$ is not diagonalizable on any spectral subspace).

Questions:

(a) Is the presence of an infinite-dimensional Jordan-block structure in $A$ necessary for the failure of $C^1$ linearization? Equivalently, does there exist a counterexample $(A, f)$ to $C^1$ linearization on some Banach space (or Hilbert space) $X$ in which $A$ is selfadjoint (in the Hilbert space case) or, more generally, normal?

(b) If no such counterexample exists when $A$ is selfadjoint (respectively, normal), can the spectral non-resonance condition above be weakened in those cases, i.e. can one establish $C^1$ linearization for selfadjoint (or normal) hyperbolic $A$ under a weaker spectral gap condition than $b < a^2$ and $A_u > B_u^{1/2}$?
artifact.status_search_result: No published resolution of this question was found. The problem is posed as an open problem about $C^1$ linearization in Banach spaces, and a brief web search did not return results indicating that either part (existence of selfadjoint/normal counterexamples or improvement of the non-resonance condition under selfadjointness/normality) has been settled.

status_evidence.title: Selfadjoint operators on real or complex Banach spaces
status_evidence.snippet: Discusses selfadjointness in general Banach space settings but does not address C^1 linearization counterexamples.
status_evidence.claim: No direct resolution of the linearization question for selfadjoint/normal A appears in the literature surfaced by search.
